Let’s check the table.  

Away teams and their scores:  
1. St Kilda – 9.11 (65) → total points 65, score notation 9.11 (goals.behinds). “Greater than 10” here means total points > 10? Or goals > 10? Usually in these questions, “score” means total points. But the statement says “score greater than 10” — all teams have total points > 10 except possibly none. Wait, 65 > 10, 66 > 10, 111 > 10, 63 > 10, 98 > 10, 58 > 10. So all 6 away teams have total points > 10.  

But maybe they mean “score greater than 10” in the goals part? The notation is goals.behinds (goals > 10)? Let’s check goals for away teams:  
St Kilda: 9 goals (not >10)  
North Melbourne: 9 goals (not >10)  
Richmond: 17 goals (>10)  
South Melbourne: 8 goals (not >10)  
Geelong: 15 goals (>10)  
Melbourne: 8 goals (not >10)  

So only Richmond and Geelong have goals > 10. That’s 2 out of 6 away teams.  

“More than half” means > 3 teams. 2 is not > 3.  

Thus statement is false.  

Final Answer: No
